## Evaluating the spatio-temporal dynamics of low- and mid-trophic level resources in the Azores: implications for the new MPA network and cetacean populations

**Summary**

This thesis investigates the spatial and temporal distribution of epipelagic low- and mid-trophic level biomass in the Azores using outputs from the ecological model **SEAPODYM-LMTL**. The study explores how productivity patterns influence marine megafauna distribution and evaluates whether the Azorean **Marine Protected Area (MPA) network** overlaps with highly productive regions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Keywords**

SEAPODYM-LMTL • trophic levels • productivity zones • marine protected areas • cetaceans

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Methods

-   Ecological model outputs from **SEAPODYM-LMTL**
-   Analysis of **three productivity indicators**
    -   Net Primary Production (NPP)\
    -   Zooplankton biomass\
    -   Micronekton biomass
-   **Time series analysis** (1998–2023)
-   **Spatial analysis** of productivity hotspots
-   Classification of **productivity zones**
    -   recurrent\
    -   occasional\
    -   unfavorable
-   Comparison with **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)**
-   **Cetacean sightings dataset** from the POPA program (2001–2015)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Key Results

::: {style="text-align: left;"}
-   **Strong spatial heterogeneity** in marine productivity across the Azores.
:::

![](files/Master_thesis/productivity.png){width="70%"}

::: {style="text-align: left;"}
-   A **high-productivity region** was identified around the islands and **north of 37°N**.
:::

![](files/Master_thesis/productivity_zones.png){width="70%"}

::: {style="text-align: left;"}
-   **Fully protected MPAs** tend to overlap with **more productive waters**, especially between **April and November**.
:::

![](files/Master_thesis/MPA_productivity.png){width="70%"}

::: {style="text-align: left;"}
-   **Baleen whales** were more frequently observed in **occasional productivity zones**, particularly during summer.
-   No clear association was detected for **dolphins** and **deep-diving cetaceans**.
:::

![](files/Master_thesis/Cetaceans_productivity.png){width="70%"}
